meaning/line.why: Both call 'online' -> 'on the line' a rewording at severity 0, which fits; Y calls 'online' a contraction, a loose word but harmless.

meaning/minute.why: Reworded (X) or same (Y) at severity 0; both fine for a host introducing the next caller.

meaning/whole.why: Both say same, severity 0, with sensible reasons.

noticeable.why: 'next one on the line should be Julien' reads naturally on a call; nothing would look wrong. X says yes.

stakes.why: Both say no; the two phrasings mean the same here.

rule.why: The words do differ, but the label 'different content word' overstates a rewording with no meaning change (and Whisper's 'on' is not plainly 'right'); both accept it fully.

blind.why: X picks 'on the line' in both orders with a sensible reason (either is plausible, and the reference may be the odd one). Y's pick flips with the order.

rank.why: Parakeet wrote exactly the reference's 'online'; X ranks it below Qwen3 and claims it 'adds extra words', which is false. Y puts Parakeet first, Qwen3 second, Whisper's bare 'on' last.

misses.why: Both find challenging->changing and performer->pro forma (where the reference is the one that is wrong). Variant/variance/varying are mishearings of a name (Varian), so trivial. Y adds Dan/Ben, Johan/Joran and 'pre prepared', all trivial. Neither notes the engine adds the caller's name where the reference has a gap.

overall.why: X's two clear mistakes (calling the slip noticeable, and ranking the exact-match engine second with a false reason) outweigh Y's flip in the blind test; X's tighter miss list is a smaller gain.
